Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned AGA for the State and learned counsel for the informant and perused the material placed on record.

The present criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed by the appellant to set aside the impugned order dated 27.07.2023, whereby the Special Judge, SC/ST Act/Additional Sessions Judge, Lalitpur has rejected the bail application of the appellant moved by him in Case Crime No. 99 of 2023, under Sections 376, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)V SC/ST Act, Police Station Narahat, District Lalitpur.

sentences.text: 1 Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
The incident is said to have taken place on 28.06.2023 while the first information report has been lodged on 13.07.2023.
The distance of the police station from the house of the informant is about 12 kms only.
No explanation has been offered for such inordinate delay.
It is also submitted that the statement of the witness Arushi is manipulated while she did not witness the incident.
Her name does not find place as witness in the FIR.
It is submitted that present elected Gram Pradhan is having enmity with the appellant and with the connivance of the prosecutrix, he has implicated the appellant in the present case.
The land of the appellant and the victim are adjacent to each other and the victim wanted to encroach the land of the appellant.
It is a case of malicious prosecution under the provisions of S.C./S.T. Act.
Appellant is languishing in jail since 14.07.2023 having no criminal history.
In case, the appellant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. assisted by learned counsel for the informant has supported the order passed by the Sessions court and vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the appellant and argued that in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. the prosecutrix has corroborated the version of the prosecution and stated that Arushi the daughter of her Jethani, witnessed the incident and narrated to her mother Dhankunwar, who narrated the incident to her husband Akhilesh and thereafter informed the husband of the prosecutrix.
The prosecutrix in her statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. have been consistently corroborated the version of the FIR.
The witness Arushi is the eye witness of the incident who has corroborated the incident in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
It appears from the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and from perusal of material on record that the court below has properly considered the case of the appellant.
Hence, in view of above consideration, the order of rejection of bail passed by the court below dated 27.07.2023 is affirmed.

Having considered the submissions of the parties noted above, finding no force in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant; without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the opinion that the appellant is not entitled to be enlarged on bail and the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
The criminal appeal is dismissed.
However, the trial court is directed to record the statement of victim and other witnesses of fact within three months from the date of production of certified copy of this order.

It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The trial court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything said in this order.

Order Date :- 18.9.2023 Mohit  Guthalu @ Rajjan Lodhi vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98607747/
